fields.name: name
fields.coerce: none: used as an object key in `magiportations`
fields.description: The mage who sent the offer: the `name` of the `magiport` event that you got.

responses.name: Success
responses.when: The offer is open, and the server found a safe spot near the mage. The teleport itself happens 400 ms later (see Also sent).

failures.intro: The server deletes the offer before the checks of rows 3 and 4. Thus, after one of these failures, the offer is gone.

rows.when: The mage did not send you an offer (`magiportations[name][you]`), the offer is used, or the mage is not online.

extra.name: name
extra.description: The `name` from the request. It is absent when the request has no `name`.

confirm.note: `magiport_gone` is a plain emit; `inviter_gone` goes through `fail_response`

rows.when: The `mount` flag of your instance is not the same as that of the instance of the mage: one of you is in the bank and the other is not.
You or the mage is in a generated map (a dream cave, `generated_magiport_allowed`), or `safe_xy_nearby` found no free spot near the mage.

also.summary: Your state with the new condition `s.magiport` `{ms: 400, x, y, f, in, map}`: the destination and the name of the mage in `f`.

also.when: Later: the `magiport` condition ends (400 ms). The server moves you to the spot with `effect: "magiport"`. It does not move you if a `fieldgen0` monster is less than 300 px from the spot.
also.summary: The map of the mage, with your new `x` and `y`. A `player` update follows.

also.when: Later, instead of `new_map`: a `fieldgen0` monster is less than 300 px from the spot.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The field generator stopped the teleport.

order: after 400 ms: `new_map` and `player` to you (or `ui` `dampened` to clients nearby)
